overall: Atlanta has warmed steadily through the morning, reaching a running max of 82.4°F by 13:00, but temperatures have since stalled with zero velocity and the current reading of 80.6°F sits 1.8°F below that running high. The modest dewpoint of 59°F and light winds of 4.6 mph are not particularly limiting factors, but the flat-to-falling trend at 13:15 — still ahead of typical peak heating hours of 2–4 PM ET — suggests the atmosphere may be losing its daytime heating drive earlier than expected.
forecast_obs_notes: The observed running max of 82.4°F has already surpassed three of the four model forecasts (ECMWF 80.6, GFS 81.9, NBM 79.6), leaving only HRRR at 83.2°F still above current observed levels; this broad under-forecasting by the cooler models combined with the stalled velocity suggests the day is running warmer than consensus but may not have enough momentum left to reach HRRR's target.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked at 82.4°F, velocity at zero, and current temps already retreating from the peak, the final high is likely very close to what has already been observed. A marginal additional push toward 82.5–83.0°F is possible if daytime heating resumes in the early afternoon, but the ensemble signals (even model 82–83°F at only 6% confidence; odd model already beaten at 81–82°F) and the stalling trend argue against a significant further rise. Best estimate is 82.5°F with moderate confidence, essentially treating the current running max as near-final.
